definitions.explanation: Pushing or rolling one's sleeves up to bare the arms, literally before work or washing, and figuratively as a sign of being ready to get down to a job.

examples.japanese: {腕|うで}まくり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{腕|うで}まくり⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{皿|さら}→皿：00883_sara⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{洗|あら}った→洗う：00827_arau⟧。
examples.english: My father rolled up his sleeves and did the dishes.

examples.japanese: 「⟦さあ→さあ：02904_saa⟧、⟦やる→やる：02980_yaru⟧ぞ」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{腕|うで}まくり⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大掃除|おおそうじ}→大掃除：08347_oosouji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: Saying "Right, let's do this," I rolled up my sleeves and started a big clean of the room.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{腕|うで}→腕：01006_ude⟧ "arm" and ⟦まくり→まくる：19421_makuru⟧, from ⟦まくる→まくる：19421_makuru⟧ "to roll up." As in English, it often signals eagerness to start: {腕|うで}まくり⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧, to be raring to go.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腕|うで}まくり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to roll up one's sleeves
- ⟦{袖|そで}→袖：02217_sode⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦まくる→まくる：19421_makuru⟧: to roll up one's sleeves (the plain verb phrase)
- {腕|うで}まくり⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{待|ま}ち{構|かま}える→待ち構える：32430_machikamaeru⟧: to wait raring to go
